──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n///\n/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Outcome {\n    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n    Success,\n    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n    Failure,\n    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n    Timeout,\n    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n    AgentNotFound,\n    /// Exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) — agent was interrupted.\n    Interrupted,\n    /// Negative exit code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n    Crash(i32),\n}\n\nimpl Outcome {\n    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n    ///\n    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n    ///\n    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - all other → `Failure`\n    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n        if was_interrupted {\n            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n        }\n\n        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n        match exit_code {\n            // Success\n            0 => Outcome::Success,\n            // Explicit failure code\n            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n            // Failure range: 2-123\n            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionMode\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n///\n/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n///   and consecutive failure count.\n///\n/// # When to use each mode\n///\n/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n///\n/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n///\n/// # API boundary\n///\n/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n/// activated. No other code should check timeout status or exit codes to make\n/// this decision — all decomposition logic should route through this enum.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum DecompositionMode {\n    /// Timeout-driven decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// Contains timeout-specific context for use in generating child bead\n    /// proposals (e.g., original timeout value, elapsed time, progress indicators).\n    Timeout {\n        /// The timeout duration that was exceeded (in seconds).\n        timeout_seconds: u64,\n        /// Optional hint about what phase was being worked on when timeout occurred.\n        /// This can be used to name the first child bead (e.g., \"Phase 1: Routing Rules\").\n        current_phase_hint: Option<String>,\n    },\n    /// Ordinary failure mode — no decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Used for all non-timeout failures where splitting the bead into child\n    /// beads would not help. The bead should be retried, released, or escalated\n    /// via the normal failure-handling path.\n    OrdinaryFailure,\n}\n\nimpl DecompositionMode {\n    /// Returns true if this is timeout decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the decomposition path.\n    /// All code that needs to know whether to decompose should call this method\n    /// rather than inspecting the enum directly.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(mode.is_timeout());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_timeout());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_timeout(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::Timeout { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this is ordinary failure mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the normal failure\n    /// handling path (retry, release, or escalate without decomposition).\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_ordinary_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the timeout duration if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the timeout value without\n    /// pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), Some(120));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn timeout_seconds(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => Some(*timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the current phase hint if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the optional phase hint\n    /// without pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode\n    /// or when the hint is not set.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), Some(&\"Phase 1\".to_string()));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn current_phase_hint(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                current_phase_hint, ..\n            } => current_phase_hint.as_ref(),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DecompositionMode {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => write!(f, \"timeout ({}s)\", timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => write!(f, \"ordinary_failure\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandError {\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    ConfigError(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n    WorkCreated,\n    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n    NoWork,\n    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n    Error(StrandError),\n    /// The strand was skipped because its prerequisites are not met.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"ran and found nothing\")\n    /// and `Error` (which means \"ran but failed\"). `Skipped` means \"did not\n    /// run because the environment doesn't support it\" — e.g., a strand that\n    /// requires a home bead store when the worker is configured without one.\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n    /// Candidates were found but all were excluded/assigned — short retry needed.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"truly no candidates\").\n    /// `FoundButExcluded` means \"candidates exist but this worker can't claim\n    /// them right now\" — they're assigned to other workers or blocked by labels.\n    /// This signals the worker to use short retry backoff instead of long idle.\n    FoundButExcluded,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ClaimResult / ClaimOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a single claim attempt for one bead.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum ClaimResult {\n    /// This worker successfully claimed the bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Another worker claimed the bead first.\n    RaceLost {\n        /// Assignee that won the race.\n        claimed_by: String,\n    },\n    /// The bead cannot be claimed (not open, blocked, etc.).\n    NotClaimable {\n        /// Human-readable reason.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// Claim CLI failed with a store/CLI error (distinct from race-lost).\n    ClaimError {\n        /// Human-readable error message.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Aggregate outcome after exhausting all candidates for a selection cycle.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\npub enum ClaimOutcome {\n    /// Successfully claimed a bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Raced every candidate and lost every time.\n    AllRaceLost,\n    /// The strand returned no candidates.\n    NoCandidates,\n    /// The bead store returned an error.\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BrDependency\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A bead dependency as returned from the `br`/`bf` JSON output, or from\n/// bead-rs's `bead` (`{\"blocker\": \"<id>\", \"kind\": \"blocks\"}` — a lean\n/// edge-only shape with no enriched title/status/priority). The aliases\n/// below accept both without changing how bf/br JSON deserializes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct BrDependency {\n    #[serde(alias = \"blocker\")]\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub title: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub status: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    #[serde(rename = \"dependency_type\", alias = \"kind\", default)]\n    pub dependency_type: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?;\n    Ok(s.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()))\n}\n\n/// A comment on a bead.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Comment {\n    /// Comment ID (internal database ID).\n    pub id: i64,\n    /// The bead this comment is on.\n    #[serde(rename = ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n//      /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// telemetry.clone();\n\n        // VALIDATION: Warn loudly if Splice is enabled but report_workspace is unset.\n        // This is a critical configuration gap - without report_workspace, Splice will\n        // silently fail to create escalation beads, missing the entire point of detection.\n        if config.strands.splice.enabled && config.strands.splice.report_workspace.is_none() {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                \"━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━\\\n                 \\n\\\n                 Splice strand is ENABLED but strands.splice.report_workspace is NOT SET!\\\n                 \\n\\\n                 Worker failure and live-loop detection will NOT create escalation beads.\\\n                 \\n\\\n                 To fix, add to your ~/.config/needle/config.yaml:\\\n                 \\n\\\n                   strands:\\\n                     splice:\\\n                       report_workspace: /path/to/your/workspace\\\n                 \\n\\\n                 Or set NEEDLE_STRANDS__SPLICE__REPORT_WORKSPACE=/path/to/workspace\\\n                 \\n\\\n                 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        let splice = SpliceStrand::new(\n            config.strands.splice.clone(),\n            splice_heartbeat_dir,\n            state_base.join(\"splice\"),\n            telemetry,\n        );\n\n        let knot = KnotStrand::new(config.strands.knot.clone(), runner_telemetry.clone());\n        StrandRunner {\n            strands: vec![\n                Box::new(pluck),\n                Box::new(mend),\n                Box::new(explore),\n                Box::new(weave),\n                Box::new(unravel),\n                Box::new(pulse),\n                Box::new(reflect),\n                Box::new(splice),\n                Box::new(knot),\n            ],\n            telemetry: runner_telemetry,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Run the waterfall, returning a `SelectOutcome` that carries the winning\n    /// candidate (if any) plus restart diagnostics.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the full `Bead` (including its workspace path) so the caller\n    /// can create the correct bead store for remote beads found by Explore.\n    /// The accompanying `String` is the name of the strand that produced the\n    /// candidate.\n    ///\n    /// When a strand returns `WorkCreated`, the waterfall restarts from Pluck.\n    /// A restart cap prevents infinite loops (e.g. a strand that always creates\n    /// work without producing a claimable bead).\n    pub async fn select(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,\n    ) -> Result<SelectOutcome> {\n        const MAX_RESTARTS: u32 = 3;\n        let mut restarts = 0u32;\n        let mut restart_triggers: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let mut strand_evaluations: Vec<StrandEvaluation> = Vec::new();\n\n        'waterfall: loop {\n            for strand in &self.strands {\n                let strand_name = strand.name().to_string();\n                let strand_span = tracing::info_span!(\n                    \"strand.{}\",\n                    strand_name,\n                    needle.strand.name = %strand_name,\n                );\n                let start = Instant::now();\n                let result = strand\n                    .evaluate(store, exclusions)\n                    .instrument(strand_span.clone())\n                    .await;\n                let elapsed_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n\n                // The remaining evaluation bookkeeping is synchronous, so a\n                // scoped guard is safe here and preserves strand context on its\n                // tracing events without crossing an `.await`.\n                let _strand_enter = strand_span.enter();\n\n                // Record strand evaluation result as span attribute.\n                let (result_str, should_record) = match &result {\n                    StrandResult::BeadFound(beads) => {\n                        let count = beads.len();\n                        (\n                            format!(\"{}({})\", strand_results::BEAD_FOUND, count),\n                            count > 0,\n                        )\n                    }\n                    StrandResult::WorkCreated => (strand_results::WORK_CREATED.to_string(), true),\n                    StrandResult::NoWork => (strand_results::NO_WORK.to_string(), true),\n                    StrandResult::Error(_) => (strand_results::ERROR.to_string(), true),\n                    StrandResult::Skipped { reason } => (format!(\"skipped({})\", reason), true),\n                    StrandResult::Split(_, _failure_count) => {\n                        (format!(\"{}({})\", strand_results::BEAD_FOUND, 1), true)\n                    }\n                    StrandResult::FoundButExcluded => (\"found_but_excluded\".to_string(), true),\n                };\n                tracing::Span::current().record(attrs::NEEDLE_STRAND_RESULT, &result_str);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(attrs::NEEDLE_STRAND_DURATION_MS, elapsed_ms);\n\n                // Set strand span status: Error for strand errors, Ok for all other results\n                // Note: Skipped is not an error - it's expected for roam-only workers\n                if matches!(result, StrandResult::Error(_)) {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", &result_str);\n                }\n\n                // Only record evaluations that produced meaningful results.\n                // Skip recording empty BeadFound results since they don't\n                // represent actual strand activity.\n                if should_record {\n                    strand_evaluations.push(StrandEvaluation {\n                        strand_name: strand_name.clone(),\n                        result: result_str.clone(),\n                        duration_ms: elapsed_ms,\n                    });\n                }\n\n                match result {\n                    StrandResult::BeadFound(beads) => {\n                        // Filter out beads that are in the exclusion set (e.g.\n                        // recently race-lost).  This prevents the waterfall from\n                        // immediately re-selecting a bead that just lost a claim\n                        // race to another worker.\n                        let original_count = beads.len();\n                        let filtered: Vec<Bead> = beads\n                            .into_iter()\n                            .filter(|b| !exclusions.contains(&b.id))\n                            .collect();\n                        let excluded_count = original_count.saturating_sub(filtered.len());\n\n                        // Record queue depth for the Pluck strand (after filtering).\n                        // This samples the current queue depth for the needle.queue.depth\n                        // observable gauge, which is measured at strand evaluation.\n                        // We report depth per priority level to enable filtered views.\n                        if strand_name == \"pluck\" {\n                            use std::collections::HashMap;\n                            let mut depths: HashMap<u8, u64> = HashMap::new();\n                            for bead in &filtered {\n                                *depths.entry(bead.priority).or_insert(0) += 1;\n                            }\n                            self.telemetry.record_queue_depth(depths);\n                        }\n\n                        if let Err(e) =\n                            self.telemetry\n                                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                                    strand_name: strand_name.clone(),\n                                    result: \"bead_found\".to_string(),\n                                    duration_ms: elapsed_ms,\n                                })\n                        {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                strand = %strand_name,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            strand = %strand_name,\n                            candidates = filtered.len(),\n                            excluded = excluded_count,\n                            elapsed_ms,\n                            \"strand found candidates\"\n                        );\n                        if let Some(bead) = filtered.into_iter().next() {\n                            return Ok(SelectOutcome {\n                                bead: Some((bead, strand_name.clone())),\n                                waterfall_restarts: restarts,\n                                restart_triggers,\n                                strand_evaluations,\n                                split_failure_count: None,\n                            });\n                        }\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    StrandResult::Split(bead, failure_count) => {\n                        let bead = *bead;\n                        if let Err(e) =\n                            self.telemetry\n                                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                                    strand_name: strand_name.clone(),\n                                    result: \"split\".to_string(),\n                                    duration_ms: elapsed_ms,\n                                })\n                        {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                strand = %strand_name,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            strand = %strand_name,\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            failure_count,\n                            \"strand triggered split for bead with excessive failures\"\n                        );\n                        return Ok(SelectOutcome {\n                            bead: Some((bead, strand_name.clone())),\n                            waterfall_restarts: restarts,\n                            restart_triggers,\n                            strand_evaluations,\n                            split_failure_count: Some(failure_count),\n                        });\n                    }\n                    StrandResult::WorkCreated => {\n                        if let Err(e) =\n                            self.telemetry\n                                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                                    strand_name: strand_name.clone(),\n                                    result: \"work_created\".to_string(),\n                                    duration_ms: elapsed_ms,\n                                })\n                        {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                strand = %strand_name,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                        restarts += 1;\n                        restart_triggers.push(strand_name.clone());\n                        if restarts > MAX_RESTARTS {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                strand = %strand_name,\n                                max_restarts = MAX_RESTARTS,\n                                \"waterfall restart cap reached, continuing to evaluate remaining strands\"\n                            );\n                            // Do NOT return None — continue evaluating remaining strands\n                            // so every strand emits telemetry and the operator can see\n                            // why the worker is idle.\n                            continue;\n                        }\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            strand = %strand_name,\n                            elapsed_ms,\n                            restart = restarts,\n                            \"strand created new work, restarting waterfall\"\n                        );\n                        continue 'waterfall;\n                    }\n                    StrandResult::NoWork => {\n                        if let Err(e) =\n                            self.telemetry\n                                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                                    strand_name: strand_name.clone(),\n                                    result: \"no_work\".to_string(),\n                                    duration_ms: elapsed_ms,\n                                })\n                        {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                strand = %strand_name,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            strand = %strand_name,\n                            elapsed_ms,\n                            \"strand returned no work\"\n                        );\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    StrandResult::Skipped { reason } => {\n                        if let Err(e) =\n                            self.telemetry\n                                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                                    strand_name: strand_name.clone(),\n                                    result: format!(\"skipped({})\", reason),\n                                    duration_ms: elapsed_ms,\n                                })\n                        {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                strand = %strand_name,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            strand = %strand_name,\n                            reason = %reason,\n                            elapsed_ms,\n                            \"strand skipped\"\n                        );\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    StrandResult::FoundButExcluded => {\n                        if let Err(e) =\n                            self.telemetry\n                                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                                    strand_name: strand_name.clone(),\n                                    result: \"found_but_excluded\".to_string(),\n                                    duration_ms: elapsed_ms,\n                                })\n                        {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                strand = %strand_name,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            strand = %strand_name,\n                            elapsed_ms,\n                            \"strand found candidates but all were excluded/assigned, triggering short retry\"\n                        );\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    StrandResult::Error(e) => {\n                        if let Err(te) =\n                            self.telemetry\n                                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                                    strand_name: strand_name.clone(),\n                                    result: \"error\".to_string(),\n                                    duration_ms: elapsed_ms,\n                                })\n                        {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                strand = %strand_name,\n                                error = %te,\n                                \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            strand = %strand_name,\n                            error = %e,\n                            elapsed_ms,\n                            \"strand error, continuing to next strand\"\n                        );\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            // All strands evaluated without finding work or triggering a restart.\n            return Ok(SelectOutcome {\n                bead: None,\n                waterfall_restarts: restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n                split_failure_count: None,\n            });\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return the names of all configured strands (for telemetry/debugging).\n    pub fn strand_names(&self) -> Vec<&str> {\n        self.strands.iter().map(|s| s.name()).collect()\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests   }\n        }\n\n        fn work_created(\n            name: &'static str,\n            count: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32>,\n        ) -> Self {\n            CountingStrand {\n {\n                StrandResult::NoWork\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn restart_cap_still_evaluates_remaining_strands() {\n        // When a strand repeatedly returns WorkCreated, the waterfall restarts.\n        // After MAX_RESTARTS, the remaining strands should still be evaluated\n        // so that operators see telemetry for every strand in the cycle.\n        let creator_count = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let observer_a_count = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let observer_b_count = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0));\n\n        let runner = StrandRunner::new(vec![\n            Box::new(CountingStrand::work_created(\n                \"creator\",\n                creator_count.clone(),\n            )),\n            Box::new(CountingStrand::no_work(\n                \"observer-a\",\n                observer_a_count.clone(),\n            )),\n            Box::new(CountingStrand::no_work(\n                \"observer-b\",\n                observer_b_count.clone(),\n            )),\n        ]);\n        let store = EmptyStore;\n        let exclusions = HashSet::new();\n        let outcome = runner.select(&store, &exclusions).await.unwrap();\n        assert!(outcome.bead.is_none());\n\n        // creator should have been evaluated MAX_RESTARTS + 1 = 4 times.\n        assert_eq!(creator_count.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst), 4);\n\n        // After the restart cap, the remaining strands should each be evaluated\n Process-group kill guard for spawned agent subprocesses.\n//!\n//! Depends on: nothing (leaf module — only `libc`).\n\nuse tokio::process::Child;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ProcessGuard\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Guard for a spawned child process that ensures cleanup on drop.\n///\n/// Wraps a `tokio::process::Child` and provides a `wait()` method. If dropped\n/// before `wait()` is called, the child process is killed to prevent orphaning.\npub struct ProcessGuard {\n    child: Option<Child>,\n    pid: u32,\n}\n\nimpl ProcessGuard {\n    /// Create a new ProcessGuard from a spawned Child.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `child` - The spawned child process to guard\n    pub fn new(child: Child) -> Self {\n        let pid = child.id().unwrap_or(0);\n        Self {\n            child: Some(child),\n            pid,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the process ID.\n    pub fn id(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.pid\n    }\n\n    /// Wait for the child to exit and return its exit status.\n    ///\n    /// This consumes the guard and returns the exit status. After calling this,\n    /// the child is considered reaped and no cleanup will be performed on drop.\n    pub async fn wait(mut self) -> std::io::Result<std::process::ExitStatus> {\n        if let Some(mut child) = self.child.take() {\n            child.wait().await\n        } else {\n            Err(std::io::Error::other(\"child already reaped\"))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get a mutable reference to the inner child (for operations like start_kill).\n    pub fn get_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Child> {\n        self.child.as_mut()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ProcessGuard {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        if let Some(mut child) = self.child.take() {\n            // Child was not waited on - kill it to prevent orphaning.\n            // Best-effort: ignore errors if already dead.\n            let _ = child.start_kill();\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ProcessGroupKillGuard\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Kills a spawned process's group on drop unless [`disarm`](Self::disarm) was\n/// called first.\n///\n/// A `tokio::time::timeout` wrapped directly around a spawn-and-wait future\n/// (e.g. `Command::output()`) kills the child correctly when *that* timeout\n/// fires: the future resolves to `Err(Elapsed)` and the caller's own match\n/// arm can react. The gap is a timeout wrapping something *further up* the\n/// call stack — Worker's mitosis-evaluation step wraps a whole multi-step\n/// `evaluate()` call (prompt build, dispatch, response parse) in its own,\n/// shorter, `tokio::time::timeout`; the weave strand does the same around its\n/// whole `evaluate_internal()`. When that outer timeout fires first, it drops\n/// the in-flight future — including whatever spawn-and-wait future was\n/// nested inside it — before any inner match arm, kill logic, or cleanup code\n/// gets a chance to run. Dropping a future mid-`Child::wait()` does not kill\n/// the OS process; the child is simply orphaned, silently, indefinitely. This\n/// guard makes that outcome unreachable: however the future is torn down,\n/// `Drop` runs and reaps the process group.    pub timestamp: String,\n}\n\nimpl TestMetrics {\n    /// Create test metrics from a test result.\n    pub fn from_result(result: &TestResult) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            status:    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Test Result\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of running cargo test.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TestResult {\n    /// The test execution status.\n    pub status: TestStatus,\n    /// Captured stdout from test execution.\n    pub stdout: String,\n    /// Captured stderr from test execution.\n    pub stderr: String,\n    /// Exit code from cargo test (None if killed by signal).\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Duration of the test run.\n    pub duration: Duration,\n}\n\n/// The status of test execution.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum TestStatus {\n    /// All tests passed successfully.\n    Success,\n    /// Some tests failed.\n    Failed,\n    /// Compilation failed.\n    CompilationFailed,\n    /// Test execution timed out.\n    TimedOut,\n}\n\nimpl TestResult {\n    /// Create a new test result from process output and duration.\n    fn from_output(output: Output, duration: Duration) -> Self {\n        let exit_code = output.status.code();\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();\n\n        let status = Self::classify_status(&output);\n\n        Self {\n            status,\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            exit_code,\n            duration,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a timeout test result with duration.\n    fn timeout(duration: Duration) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            status: TestStatus::TimedOut,\n            stdout: String::new(),\n            stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n            exit_code: None,\n            duration,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Classify the test status based on process output.\n    fn classify_status(output: &Output) -> TestStatus {\n        let exit_code = output.status.code();\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n\n        // Check for compilation errors\n        if stderr.contains(\"error[E\") || stderr.contains(\"error: aborting\") {\n            return TestStatus::CompilationFailed;\n        }\n\n        // Check exit code\n        match exit_code {\n            Some(0) => TestStatus::Success,\n            Some(101) => {\n                // Exit code 101 indicates test failures\n                if stderr.contains(\"test result:\") {\n                    TestStatus::Failed\n                } else {\n                    TestStatus::CompilationFailed\n                }\n            }\n            Some(code) => {\n                tracing::warn!(exit_code = code, \"unexpected exit code from cargo test\");\n                TestStatus::Failed\n            }\n            None => {\n                tracing::warn!(\"no exit code available from cargo test\");\n                TestStatus::Failed\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the test result indicates success.\n    pub fn is_success(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self.status, TestStatus::Success)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the test result indicates failure.\n    pub fn is_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.is_success()\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the failure was due to compilation errors.\n    pub fn is_compilation_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self.status, TestStatus::CompilationFailed)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the test timed out.\n    pub fn is_timed_out(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self.status, TestStatus::TimedOut)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns a human-readable summary of the result.\n    pub fn summary(&self) -> String {\n        match &self.status {\n            TestStatus::TimedOut => \"Test execution timed out\".to_string(),\n            TestStatus::CompilationFailed => \"Compilation failed\".to_string(),\n            TestStatus::Success => \"All tests passed\".to_string(),\n            TestStatus::Failed => {\n                format!(\"Tests failed with exit code {:?}\", self.exit_code)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the captured stdout.\n    pub fn captured_stdout(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.stdout\n    }\n\n    /// Get the captured stderr.\n    pub fn captured_stderr(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.stderr\n    }\n\n    /// Persist test output (stdout and stderr) to files.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `output_dir` - Directory where output files will be written\n    /// * `base_name` - Base name for the output files (stdout will be `base_name.stdout`, stderr will be `base_name.stderr`)\n    ///\n    /// ## Returns\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` if both files were written successfully, or an error if either write failed.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The output directory cannot be created\n    /// - Either file cannot be written\n    pub fn persist_output(&self, output_dir: &Path, base_name: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        // Create output directory if it doesn't exist\n        fs::create_dir_all(output_dir).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to create output directory: {}\",\n                output_dir.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // Write stdout\n        let stdout_path = output_dir.join(format!(\"{}.stdout\", base_name));\n        self.write_file(&stdout_path, &self.stdout)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write stdout to {}\", stdout_path.display()))?;\n\n        // Write stderr\n        let stderr_path = output_dir.join(format!(\"{}.stderr\", base_name));\n        self.write_file(&stderr_path, &self.stderr)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write stderr to {}\", stderr_path.display()))?;\n\n        tracing::debug!(\n            stdout_path = %stdout_path.display(),\n            stderr_path = %stderr_path.display(),\n            stdout_len = self.stdout.len(),\n            stderr_len = self.stderr.len(),\n            \"persisted test output\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Persist test metrics to a JSON file.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `output_dir` - Directory where the metrics file will be written\n    /// * `base_name` - Base name for the metrics file (will be `base_name.metrics.json`)\n    ///\n    /// ## Returns\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` if the metrics file was written successfully, or an error if the write failed.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The output directory cannot be created\n    /// - The file cannot be written\n    /// - The metrics cannot be serialized to JSON\n    pub fn persist_metrics(&self, output_dir: &Path, base_name: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        // Create output directory if it doesn't exist\n        fs::create_dir_all(output_dir).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to create output directory: {}\",\n                output_dir.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // Create metrics from result\n        let metrics = TestMetrics::from_result(self);\n\n        // Serialize to JSON\n        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&metrics)\n            .context(\"failed to serialize test metrics to JSON\")?;\n\n        // Write metrics file\n        let metrics_path = output_dir.join(format!(\"{}.metrics.json\", base_name));\n        self.write_file(&metrics_path, &json)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write metrics to {}\", metrics_path.display()))?;\n\n        tracing::debug!(\n            metrics_path = %metrics_path.display(),\n            status = ?metrics.status,\n            duration_ms = metrics.duration_ms,\n            \"persisted test metrics\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Persist both test output and metrics.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method that calls both `persist_output` and `persist_metrics`.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `output_dir` - Directory where files will be written\n    /// * `base_name` - Base name for the output files\n    ///\n    /// ## Returns\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` if all files were written successfully, or an error if any write failed.\n    pub fn persist_all(&self, output_dir: &Path, base_name: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        self.persist_output(output_dir, base_name)?;\n        self.persist_metrics(output_dir, base_name)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Helper method to write content to a file.\n    ///\n    /// This method handles the actual file I/O and is used by both `persist_output` and `persist_metrics`.\n    fn write_file(&self, path: &Path, content: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut file = File::create(path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        file.write_all(content.as_bytes())\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write to file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Test Runner\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Basic test runner for executing cargo test commands.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TestRunner {\n    /// Workspace directory where tests will be run.\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Timeout in seconds for test execution.\n    timeout_secs: u64,\n    /// Additional arguments to pass to cargo test.\n    extra_args: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl TestRunner {\n    /// Create a new test runner for the given workspace.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `workspace` - Path to the workspace directory\n    pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n            extra_args: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set the timeout for test execution.\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Add extra arguments to pass to cargo test.\n    pub fn with_extra_arg(mut self, arg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        self.extra_args.push(arg.into());\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test with the given additional arguments.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `args` - Additional arguments to pass to cargo test\n    ///\n    /// ## Returns\n    ///\n    /// Returns `TestResult` containing:\n    /// - `status`: The test execution status (Success, Failed, CompilationFailed, TimedOut)\n    /// - `stdout`: Captured stdout from test execution\n    /// - `stderr`: Captured stderr from test execution\n    /// - `exit_code`: Process exit code (None if killed by signal)\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n    /// - The process fails to spawn\n    pub fn run_tests(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<TestResult> {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n\n        // Build the command\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n        cmd.arg(\"test\");\n        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n        cmd.stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped());\n        cmd.stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped());\n\n        // Add extra arguments\n        for arg in &self.extra_args {\n            cmd.arg(arg);\n        }\n\n        // Add additional arguments\n        for arg in args {\n            cmd.arg(arg);\n        }\n\n        // Spawn the process\n        tracing::debug!(\n            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n            args = ?args,\n            \"spawning cargo test process\"\n        );\n\n        let result = self.execute_with_timeout(cmd)?;\n\n        let duration = start.elapsed();\n\n        // Build the test result with captured output\n        let test_result = match result {\n            Some(output) => TestResult::from_output(output, duration),\n            None => TestResult::timeout(duration),\n        };\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            status = ?test_result.status,\n            duration_secs = duration.as_secs(),\n            stdout_len = test_result.stdout.len(),\n            stderr_len = test_result.stderr.len(),\n            \"cargo test completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(test_result)\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a command with timeout protection.\n    ///\n    /// Returns Ok(Some(output)) if the command completes within timeout,\n    /// Ok(None) if the command times out, or Err if the process fails to spawn.\n    fn execute_with_timeout(&self, mut cmd: Command) -> Result<Option<Output>> {\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n\n        // Spawn the process\n        let mut child = cmd.spawn().context(\"failed to spawn cargo test process\")?;\n\n        // Wait for completion with timeout\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        loop {\n            // Check if timeout exceeded\n            if start.elapsed() > timeout {\n                tracing::error!(timeout_secs = self.timeout_secs, \"cargo test timed out\");\n\n                // Kill the child process\n                let _ = child.kill();\n                let _ = child.wait();\n\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n\n            // Try to wait with a small timeout\n            match child.try_wait() {\n                Ok(Some(_status)) => {\n                    // Process has exited\n                    return Ok(Some(child.wait_with_output()?));\n                }\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    // Still running, sleep a bit and retry\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"error waiting for cargo test: {}\", e))\n                        .context(\"failed to wait for cargo test process\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Get the extra arguments.\n    pub fn extra_args(&self) -> &[String] {\n        &self.extra_args\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_captured_output_new() {\n
